parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a national binary-document and entry-screening system—X passports no longer issued, discrepancy can trigger refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility—with this state's birth-sex facilities rule expanded in May 2026 to schools, colleges and universities. Documented bathroom trespass arrest, birth-sex custody/hormone-removal practices and immigration-custody abuse raise severity, while courts have enjoined some orders and protected one student, hate-crime and employment law exist nationally, and imprisonment is short rather than highly likely and execution is not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition; X-marker passports stopped Feb 2025, existing valid until expiry; Supreme Court allowed restriction Nov 2025; passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can become refusal, then fraud/misrepresentation inquiry and possible permanent ineligibility.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; no documented cell-placement rule for this state.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facilities enforcement could lead to detention where birth-sex and treatment restrictions apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: This state requires public school, college and university restrooms matching sex at birth, signed 15 May 2026; national map shows bans in many states and criminal trespass in four.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National appellate order required a district to allow one trans student to use boys' bathroom during litigation; Supreme Court denied pause 10 Sept 2025.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State ban operates despite national employment and hate-crime protections; relief is litigant-specific and merits unresolved.

care_services.exposure: Child gender-affirming care banned in 27 states; Jan 2025 order on minors' care; proposed rule would bar public insurance under 18; DOJ hospital subpoenas reported.
care_services.protection: Some orders blocked/enjoined; adult visitor hormone continuity rules are not documented.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor faces school, sports and care restrictions; an adult's emergency or routine care access is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DoD/DOJ framing includes 'radical gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; teacher prosecution directive for social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target people who simply disagree; reward memo never uses phrase as criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing increases official discretion at borders, schools and facilities, but documented visitor arrests remain limited to trespass-type cases.

minors_guardians.exposure: State simultaneously imposes birth-sex bathrooms in K-12 and higher education and sports ban signed 2022; parent/guardian may face school and care consequences for a trans minor.
minors_guardians.protection: One student's appellate protection during equal-protection litigation; local municipal employment protections in several places.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor encounters combined school, sports, facilities and care restrictions stronger than for adult alone.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Poll: 66% support birth-sex on documents, 69% support birth-sex sports; trans-specific visitor violence rate is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute punishes gender-identity hate crimes; only 23 states cover it in state statutes and this state has no hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public support for binary rules plus no state hate-crime law weakens local recourse, despite functioning national courts.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and health-rule litigation unresolved; state bathroom law merits undecided; travel advisories from eight governments by March 2025.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some orders and granted interim student relief; civil-liberties organisations active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but are slow, partial and state-specific, so they do not cancel universal document/facilities exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine exclusion and ineffective/no timely remedy, but higher than 0.35 because documented short jail, custody hormone removal and possible lifetime entry bar add severity, while courts provide some relief.

Similar universal document exposure and administrative harm without credible execution; this case is slightly lower due to criminal bathroom trespass, expanded higher-education ban and documented custody abuse.

Higher than this case: anchor has national equality protection, reliable release, apology and compensation after brief hold. Here passport restriction is operative nationally and facilities ban is state law, so protections are weaker.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: national binary documents and discretionary entry screening create the first outing point; state birth-sex facilities rules create continuous exposure in public buildings, schools and universities; any detention then interacts with hormone-removal and birth-sex custody practices. Courts and partial national protections mitigate but do not pre-empt these routes, and a minor adds sports, school and care restrictions. No documented execution or highly likely imprisonment, but universal exposure plus short custody and entry consequences place it below the 0.45 anchor tier.
